overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by a private discussion of a licensing matter at a caucus among a quorum, and by failing to respond to complaints properly; it declined the non-OML allegations and ordered compliance and training certification.

allegations.summary: A board member allegedly made statements about Board business to the other two members outside a noticed meeting, at a town caucus.
allegations.key_passage: The private discussion at the Town Caucus therefore violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The Board allegedly failed to formally review and respond to the Open Meeting Law complaints filed against it as required by law.
allegations.key_passage: This failure to follow proper procedures in responding the Open Meeting Law complaints at issue also violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaints alleged approval of a food permit without consulting other members, special treatment for friends, and conducting Board business on a personal computer; these are not Open Meeting Law claims.
allegations.key_passage: These allegations, if proven, would not constitute violations of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #1: Open Meeting Law Definitions and certify to the AG's office within thirty (30) days of the letter.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Additionally, we order the Board to review the Attorney General's Open Meeting Law Training Video #1: Open Meeting Law Definitions and certify to our office within thirty (30) days of this letter
